cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you replace your code review with feedback loops
cards.claim: Replacing code review with production feedback loops and not reading the code leads to an unrecoverable 3am outage and possibly company death.
cards.evidence_detail: Hypothetical failure narrative, no data.
cards.landing: Keep human code reading as a gate in the phase routine; argues against dropping the Opus reviewer or owner view

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: stuff might break at 3am and if you're relying on loops to fix it
cards.claim: For the next 1-3 years, systems will break at 3am and loop-based fixing without human understanding of the code is an existential threat.
cards.evidence_detail: Forecast stated in quoted tweet.
cards.landing: Runbook and cold-resume (P1): a human or fresh agent must be able to understand the code; supports knowledge-store and handoff docs

cards.source_title: Why review agents do not solve slop
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: too easy to oversteer with "is this code good" or "is this code bad"
cards.claim: Code review agents are unreliable because a binary good/bad prompt is easily oversteered, so they do not solve the too-much-AI-code problem.
cards.evidence_detail: Argued from the sycophancy/flip-flop quoted post (60% flip rate cited by quoted author, not Dex).
cards.landing: Reviewer prompt design: Opus reviewer is refute-by-default with per-register-id fail-before/pass-after, which is rule-grounded rather than 'is this good'
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Why review agents do not solve slop

cards.source_title: Why review agents do not solve slop
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: why weren't those rules / guidelines grounded in your original plan?
cards.claim: Objective review rules should already be grounded in the original plan rather than invented at review time.
cards.evidence_detail: Rhetorical question, no data.
cards.landing: Ship-plan phase routine: put acceptance rules in the plan at 'Plan @ sha' so the reviewer checks against them
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Why review agents do not solve slop

cards.source_title: Why review agents do not solve slop
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: There is something to be said for "throw more tokens at the problem"
cards.claim: Throwing more tokens at verification can work, but only if done thoughtfully.
cards.evidence_detail: Qualified statement, no data.
cards.landing: Verifier effort routing (xhigh vs medium) and refuter panels
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Why review agents do not solve slop

cards.source_title: Why review agents do not solve slop
cards.author: other
cards.quote: GPT, Claude, and Gemini flip their answers ~60% of the time
cards.claim: Quoted study says frontier models reverse answers ~60% of the time under mere user doubt, which Dex uses to explain why review agents are unreliable.
cards.evidence_detail: Claimed 2025 study cited by Randal Olson; Dex endorses implicitly by quoting; not verified.
cards.landing: Reviewer/refuter prompts: avoid leading 'are you sure' re-asks; fresh-context refuters
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Why review agents do not solve slop

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: roughly the same length and detail as the code itself
cards.claim: A spec detailed enough to reliably generate quality code is about as long and detailed as the code, so reviewing it adds little over reviewing the code.
cards.evidence_detail: Endorses Gabriella Gonzalez's blog post; no numbers.
cards.landing: Ship plan: plans/specs should not be reviewed as a substitute for code; keep plan short and review code
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Spec is the new code is not enough

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you ABSOLUTELY SHOULD care about the code at that level of abstraction
cards.claim: Except for prototypes and side projects, engineers should still read and care about code, even for zero-to-one software.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated position.
cards.landing: Owner view and reviewer expectations; human code reading stays in loop
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Spec is the new code is not enough

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: lets you resteer the model *before* it slops out N-thousand LOC
cards.claim: The safe way to gain leverage over coding agents is a mechanism that lets you resteer before large code is generated, not a spec and not AskUserQuestion rounds.
cards.evidence_detail: Points to unnamed mechanism; teased QRSPI work.
cards.landing: Phase routine: early checkpoint (draft PR with 'Plan @ sha' and decisions journal) before implementation
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Spec is the new code is not enough

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the word "spec" is broken anyway
cards.claim: The word spec is overloaded and unhelpful; the resteering mechanism should not be called or built as a spec.
cards.evidence_detail: Terminology claim.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (naming of plan documents)
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Spec is the new code is not enough

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: i own the execution, and give little things to the agent
cards.claim: The conservative option is to own execution yourself and delegate small pieces to the agent while checking along the way.
cards.evidence_detail: Described as the 'decel' default.
cards.landing: Phase sizing: small delegated units with checks
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 — Spec is the new code is not enough

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: many folks struggle to keep it on task past 100k
cards.claim: A 1M context window is not useful because people struggle to keep models on task past roughly 100k tokens.
cards.evidence_detail: Older quoted tweet about Sonnet 4; re-shared with 'don't make me tap the sign'.
cards.landing: One phase per new session; compaction/context budget guidance (~100k working limit)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: shifting away from "token harder" to "token smarter"
cards.claim: The AI coding meta is moving from maximizing token spend to spending tokens more smartly.
cards.evidence_detail: Observation across circles, naming Ralph wiggum, RPI, conductor, cmux as the August 'token harder' wave.
cards.landing: Effort routing: do not default verifiers to xhigh

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: rarely hit 50% of claude max quota
cards.claim: His team went from 3k per engineer raw token spend to rarely using 50% of a Claude Max quota because they care about avoiding slop architecture.
cards.evidence_detail: Self-reported, with footnote 'probably still moving faster than you'; no measurement.
cards.landing: Cost/effort routing in Workflow scripts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you are being held back by your inability to spend tokens
cards.claim: The August 2025 mandate was to spend many tokens via Ralph wiggum loops, RPI, and parallel worktree tools, which he now treats as the wrong emphasis.
cards.evidence_detail: Retrospective characterisation.
cards.landing: Workflow orchestration: parallel fan-out only where it earns its cost

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: here have some alpha on what we've been working on the last few months
cards.claim: HumanLayer has a QRSPI method (linked hlyr.dev/qrspi-mlops) as the successor to RPI, held back for AI Engineer Miami.
cards.evidence_detail: Link only; the target page was not read in this task.
cards.landing: Phase routine design: check linked QRSPI material for question/design/structure stages

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: slop in → slop out
cards.claim: AI can write specs and PRDs, but outsourcing the thinking produces garbage, so the human input quality still determines output quality.
cards.evidence_detail: Promo for an AITW episode with Vaibhav on techniques for getting good specs from agents.
cards.landing: Plan authoring step: human supplies the intent, agent drafts; episode content not read

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: STOP WRITING YOUR SPECS BY HAND
cards.claim: Specs and PRDs should be generated by coding agents with good techniques rather than hand-written in markdown.
cards.evidence_detail: Episode promotion; techniques not described in the tweet.
cards.landing: Skill for spec/plan drafting under .claude/skills/

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: move 2-3x faster across the entire SDLC (not just coding)
cards.claim: HumanLayer claims 2-3x speedup across the whole SDLC while keeping rigorous architecture and design standards.
cards.evidence_detail: Product copy; no method or data.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: building blocks for your software factory
cards.claim: HumanLayer positions itself as an agentic IDE, collaboration platform and components for building a software factory; RPI is deployed at Block and Uber.
cards.evidence_detail: Customer names asserted, no data.
cards.landing: Reusable workflow library idea (building blocks)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we can prompt our way around split brain for most things
cards.claim: The split-brain problem of sub-agents can mostly be solved by prompting, though long context is sometimes needed in exceptional cases.
cards.evidence_detail: Reply in a thread; head tweet only captured.
cards.landing: Custom agent prompts (fixflow-explorer) and subagent handoff format

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: user -> Claude -> task() input -> subagent behavior -> subagent response format
cards.claim: Subagent use chains user, parent Claude, task input, subagent behaviour and response format, like a game of telephone where each hop can distort.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes the 'triple pendulum' of context management.
cards.landing: Specify subagent input and return format explicitly in agent files and Workflow scripts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: why we should still read the code, and how to design your software factory
cards.claim: The 'why software factories fail' talk argues engineers should still read code and covers how to design a software factory.
cards.evidence_detail: Promo tweet; 300k views stated; video content not read here.
cards.landing: Video is a separate source for another reader; points to verifier/backpressure design

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: walk through research/plan/impl with the legendary @vaibcode
cards.claim: AITW #33 demonstrates the research/plan/impl flow inside CodeLayer by building three real features (AI session titles, summaries, Obsidian editor support).
cards.evidence_detail: Announcement only; episode content not captured.
cards.landing: Episode itself is the evidence of RPI in practice; this tweet is a pointer
